source_records.source_title: Disclosure under Regulation 30: financial loss arising from fraud incident at Starmangalsutra Private Limited

summary: Sky Gold & Diamonds disclosed on 16 July 2026 that its subsidiary Starmangalsutra Private Limited had lost approximately ₹10.70 crore after unknown persons reportedly compromised an employee’s company-issued mobile and laptop and used deepfake methods, including profile cloning, to impersonate a director. Believing the purported instructions were genuine, an employee transferred funds from the subsidiary’s bank account to unknown accounts; the director later confirmed that no such instructions had been given. The company said it discovered the incident on 15 July, reported it to cybercrime authorities, and asked banks to trace and freeze beneficiary accounts. It reported no indication of a wider network or database breach and no material business disruption. The exact synthetic medium, compromise path, recovered amount and investigative outcome remain unestablished. The company attributed a short disclosure delay to fact checking and coordination with banks and authorities. It said it was reviewing employee awareness, verification protocols and internal controls and would strengthen them.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The 16 July listed-company disclosure directly establishes what Sky Gold reported: approximately ₹10.70 crore in subsidiary loss, an employee’s transfers on purported director instructions, later denial by the director, 15 July discovery, and cybercrime and bank recovery steps. The company attributes the attack to compromised issued devices and advanced deepfake methods including profile cloning and coercion; no underlying forensic artefact identifies a model, synthetic audio/video modality, access path or precise sequence. The Economic Times independently reports the disclosure and amount, but largely depends on the company’s account rather than an independent technical investigation. AIID catalogues one underlying report. Actual freezing or recovery, criminal findings, and wider data impact beyond the company’s stated lack of indication remain unknown.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: Human attackers reportedly used a cloned representation of the director to supply false payment authority, and the employee transferred funds. The deceptive economic request and the unauthorised use of the director’s identity representation are separate mechanisms. The company’s description supports the latter at medium confidence even though the exact source media and generator are unpublished. No autonomous AI objective, preexisting safeguard failure or eventual recovery amount is established. Company-reported director impersonation and subsequent denial support separate economic, likeness and social-engineering failures, while production modality, interaction, compromise path and recovery remain unpublished. Independent OECD autonomy/privacy/dignity assessment is Not aligned for the company-reported false director representation and resulting transfers. Autonomous/interactive-system transparency, affective modelling and later statutory-source candidates remain audit-only because their specific objects/timing are not established. No hidden generator safeguard or eventual recovery is inferred. The reported cloned director profile materially executed the false instruction; the employee transferred funds believing it genuine, and the director denied issuing it. This independently establishes impaired choice under the human-directed scope of the current manipulation criteria, without asserting an autonomous AI objective.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The reported cloned director identity was used to make a false payment instruction credible. A separate consent boundary arises when an identifiable person’s profile is reused to portray that person in a transaction they did not authorise. The issuer’s account supports these two mechanisms without specifying the deepfake’s technical medium.
